examples.purpose: The provider on the Buy Gold screen, the guide’s In context: a Title, the Card Provider Info with the provider’s name and logo, and the screen’s own Buy Button below it. The URI stands for the provider’s logo, and onPress for the screen starting the purchase. The guide’s card has four facts as StatItem children; StatItem has no entry in this pack, so they are left out and the card shows its header alone: report that the facts need StatItem.
examples.jsx:
<VStack>
  <Title title="Buy gold" subtitle="24K, stored in an insured vault" />
  <CardProviderInfo
    label="Gold"
    imageSource={{ uri: 'https://example.com/jio-gold-logo.png' }}
  />
  <Button label="Buy gold" onPress={() => {}} />
</VStack>

from.quote: The screen supplies the provider’s logo, name, and facts.

examples.purpose: A pressable card, the guide’s Pressable: onPress makes the whole card one button that looks the same as the default, named by accessibilityLabel or else by label. The accessibilityLabel is the one the guide’s code gives its Pressable card (the rendered copy doesn’t show it). onPress stands for the screen’s response to the press, and the URI for the provider’s logo. The facts (StatItem children) are left out, as above.

/>

props.name: label
props.description: Product name shown in the ProductLabel header. Default "Gold", from the component source.

props.name: imageSource
props.description: Image source for the product avatar. Omit to show the label without a portrait.

props.name: showAvatar
props.description: showAvatar={true} with no imageSource shows a plain neutral 29 px circle, not a picture; left unset, no imageSource means no avatar. Declared: Show the header avatar. Defaults to on only when `imageSource` is set. Pass `false` to hide an avatar that has an image.

props.name: children
props.description: Children get the card’s modes and sit two per row, each in an equal cell. Declared: Slot content — typically StatItem components arranged in a 2-column grid.

props.name: onPress
props.description: With onPress the card is a Pressable with role button, named accessibilityLabel, or else label; it has no pressed, hover or disabled look. Declared: Press handler for the whole card. When set, the card becomes pressable (rendered through a `Pressable` with `accessibilityRole="button"`).

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accessibility label forwarded to the pressable wrapper (defaults to `label`).

modes.name: AppearanceBrand
modes.description: A token collection CardProviderInfo reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

modes.name: Avatar Size
modes.description: The card’s header (ProductLabel) sets Avatar Size S unless modes set one, so the logo is 29 px, Figma’s size; L is 42, M 36, XS 14.
